title: EventDiffusion: Learning Native Event Stream Distribution from Videos
abstract: arXiv:2611.33096v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Event cameras capture asynchronous brightness changes at high temporal resolution, but scarce recordings constrain data-driven research. Sparse RGB observations cannot uniquely determine intervening events since identical frames may correspond to streams with different activity, polarities, and timing. Existing simulators largely rely on prescribed sensor dynamics and estimated brightness trajectories, whose assumptions limit the diversity and fidelity of plausible event streams. We introduce EventDiffusion, a hierarchical generative framework that directly learns the conditional distribution of native asynchronous event streams from real recordings. EventDiffusion decomposes generation into three probabilistic processes: Event Activity Diffusion (EAD) learns stochastic discrete event counts; Event Spatial Allocation (ESA) distributes these counts to individual pixels while preserving cardinality; and Event Timing Diffusion (ETD) learn

translated_title: EventDiffusion：从视频中学习原生事件流分布
translated_abstract: 事件相机能够以高时间分辨率捕获异步的亮度变化，但稀缺的真实记录数据限制了数据驱动研究的发展。稀疏的RGB观测无法唯一地确定其间发生的事件，因为相同的帧可能对应于具有不同活动强度、极性和时序的事件流。现有的模拟器主要依赖预设的传感器动态模型和估计的亮度轨迹，这些假设限制了合理事件流的多样性和保真度。我们提出了EventDiffusion，一个层次化的生成框架，直接从真实记录中学习原生异步事件流的条件分布。EventDiffusion将生成过程分解为三个概率过程：事件活动扩散（EAD）学习随机的离散事件计数；事件空间分配（ESA）将这些计数分配到各个像素上并保持基数不变；事件时序扩散（ETD）学习……
tldr: EventDiffusion提出了一种层次化生成框架，通过事件活动扩散、事件空间分配和事件时序扩散三个概率过程，直接从真实记录中学习原生异步事件流的条件分布，从而从视频中生成多样且逼真的事件流。
en_tdlr: EventDiffusion introduces a hierarchical generative framework that decomposes event stream generation into three probabilistic processes—Event Activity Diffusion, Event Spatial Allocation, and Event Timing Diffusion—to directly learn the conditional distribution of native asynchronous event streams from real recordings.
